title: IBM OM standard-crossbar fresh-array smoke with published defective cells
hypothesis: Retaining the IBM-OM preset's published stuck/corrupt cells instead of replacing them with healthy donor identities will cause a greater-than-two-percentage-point apparent-forward loss against the matched repaired-array smoke in at least one source or target assignment, even though every active state continues to use its sampled intrinsic reference through q=a-r.
motivation: The completed fresh-array smoke used counterfactual repair and therefore measured normal device variation and stochastic programming without surviving defective cells. This extension changes only the corruption policy to published, keeps the exact source and target assignments and endpoint streams, and pairs every metric with study mnist-ibm-om-crossbar-fresh-array-smoke-20260830-v1. It tests whether the repaired direct and continuous-HWA portability result, and the QAT transfer failure, persist when sampled stuck devices remain in place.

arms.description: Exact teacher master, no off-chip updates, with published stuck/corrupt cells retained on the source and three untouched targets.
Five one-minibatch HWA epochs and target-specific support mapping with the published defective identities retained.
Five one-minibatch deterministic-QAT epochs and target-specific codebook projection with published defective identities retained.

completion_criteria: All three declared configs complete exactly once and record the identical teacher, source assignment 87004, source endpoint seeds 89402-89405, target assignments 87005-87007, target endpoint seeds 89502-89705, data limit of 16 off-chip examples, and evaluation limit of the first 1000 official MNIST test examples used by the repaired smoke.

Each published-defect config is semantically identical to its matched repaired config except that device.corruption_policy changes from counterfactual_repaired to published; model, mapping, training, recovery, transfer, and evaluation settings must match exactly.

For every source and target assignment, the run records the sampled published-corrupt mask and count, final surviving-corrupt mask and count, total active-state count, defect fraction, population fingerprint, and per-tile counts; published policy must leave the sampled corrupt identities in the final population rather than drawing repair donors.

The sampled published-corrupt masks and base binding-construction seeds match those of the same assignments in repaired study mnist-ibm-om-crossbar-fresh-array-smoke-20260830-v1, while the effective population fingerprints reflect the declared corruption-policy intervention.

Every source and target reports target-specific no-write mapped accuracy and all four post-write apparent-forward and hidden-persistent accuracies separately, together with programming acceptance, saturation, corrupt-device acceptance, budget-exhaustion, pulse-count, and requested/realized hash diagnostics.

This smoke performs no on-chip optimizer update, does not alter the completed repaired study or its artifacts, and is not finalized as production evidence about fabricated defect rates or on-chip-learning necessity.
analysis_plan: Pair each published-defect arm with the corresponding repaired arm from mnist-ibm-om-crossbar-fresh-array-smoke-20260830-v1 by frozen-master role, assignment seed, and endpoint-seed position. Verify the common teacher and matching non-corruption config fields before computing accuracy differences.

For source 87004 and each target 87005-87007, report published-corrupt and final-corrupt counts and fractions overall and by tile, plus corrupt-device apparent acceptance, saturation, and pulse-budget exhaustion. Keep the 39,700 programmable active states distinct from the 39,700 sampled reference values.

For every arm and assignment, report no-write target-mapped accuracy, all four apparent-forward endpoint accuracies, all four hidden-persistent endpoint accuracies, their means and ranges, and the paired published-minus-repaired differences. Apparent q remains the AIHWKit-style network state; persistent q remains a programming-state diagnostic.

Call the published defects negligible at smoke level only if, for every arm and source/target assignment, both no-write accuracy and mean apparent-forward accuracy are no more than two percentage points below the matched repaired result. Otherwise report the arm- and assignment-specific defect penalty without pooling it into programming noise.

Apply the original portability criterion independently under published defects: call an arm transfer-stable only when every target assignment's apparent-forward mean is within two percentage points of that arm's published-defect source mean. Report pooled writes only as secondary and never treat twelve writes as twelve independent arrays.

Compare the apparent-minus-persistent accuracy gap and no-write-to-apparent programming loss between published and repaired populations to distinguish stuck-cell mapping loss from stochastic endpoint loss. Do not interpret intrinsic-reference subtraction as repairing an active state whose bounds and pulse increments are stuck.

Keep the first-1000-example cohort, one-minibatch off-chip adaptation, three target arrays, model-based AIHWKit 1.1.0 evidence, lack of inference read/retention/line-resistance effects, and absence of defect-aware remapping or spare rows/columns visible as limitations.
